simple.meaning: נָשַׁךְ (nâshak) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to strike with a sting (as a serpent); figuratively, to oppress with interest on a loan.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 16 times across Genesis, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, and 4 more, beginning at Genesis 49:17. Its contexts include family, death, land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָשַׁךְ (H5391).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: נָשַׁךְ (nâshak) / H5391 is traced through Genesis 49:17, Numbers 21:6, Numbers 21:8, Numbers 21:9 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: Dan will be a serpent on the trail,
Yahweh sent venomous snakes among the people, and they bit the people. Many people of Israel died.
Yahweh said to Moses, “Make a venomous snake, and set it on a pole. It shall happen that everyone who is bitten, when he sees it, shall live.”
Moses made a serpent of bronze, and set it on the pole. If a serpent had bitten any man, when he looked at the serpent of bronze, he lived.
You may charge a foreigner interest; but you shall not your brother interest, that Yahweh your God may bless you in all that you put your hand to, in the land where you go in to possess it.
You may charge a foreigner interest; but you shall not your brother interest, that Yahweh your God may bless you in all that you put your hand to, in the land where you go in to possess it.
When you vow a vow to Yahweh your God, you shall not be slack to pay it, for Yahweh your God will surely require it of you; and it would be sin in you.
When you vow a vow to Yahweh your God, you shall not be slack to pay it, for Yahweh your God will surely require it of you; and it would be sin in you.
In the end, it bites like a snake,
He who digs a pit may fall into it; and whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.
If the snake bites before it is charmed, then is there no profit for the charmer’s tongue.
As if a man fled from a lion,

Though they hide themselves in the top of Carmel, I will search and take them out there; and though they be hidden from my sight in the bottom of the sea, there I will command the serpent, and it will bite them.
Yahweh says concerning the prophets who lead my people astray; for those who feed their teeth, they proclaim, “Peace!” and whoever doesn’t provide for their mouths, they prepare war against him:
Won’t your debtors rise up suddenly, and wake up those who make you tremble, and you will be their victim?

definitions.short: to strike with a sting (as a serpent); figuratively, to oppress with interest on a loan
definitions.full: H5391. nashak נָשַׁךְ verb bite (Late Hebrew = Biblical Hebrew, but also transposed נְכַשׁ Hiph`il); Assyrian našâku Dl HWB 486 ; נְכֵית ᵑ7 (especially of snakes); Syriac , ; Ethiopic Di 642 ; Ba ZMG xliii (1889), 188 compare Arabic , undo threads, untwist rope, disintegrate, dissolve ); — Qal Perfect 3masculine singular נָשַׁךְ Num 21:9 , suffix וּנְשָׁכוֺ consecutive Amos 5:19 , וּנְשָׁכָם consecutive 9:3 ; Imperfect 3masculine singular יִשֹּׁךְ Eccl 10:11 , יִשָּׁ֑ךְ Prov 23:32 , suffix יִשְּׁכֶנּוּ Eccl 10:8 ; Participle active נשֵׁךְ Gen 49:17 ; plural נשְׁכִים Micah 3:5 , suffix נשְׁכֶיךָ Hab 2:7 ; passive נָשׁוּךְ Num 21:8 ; — bite , chiefly of serpent, with accusative, Amos 5:19 ; 9:3 ; Gen 49:17 (poem in J), Num 21:8 (passive participle, absolute), 21:9 , Eccl 10:8 also 10:11 (absolute), Prov 23:32 (simile of wine); figurative of prophets ׳הַנּ בְּשִׁנֵּיהֶם Micah 3:5 who are biting with their teeth , and crying, Peace! figurative of oppression, etc., נשְׁכֶיךָ Hab 2:7 (with play on sense thy debtors, those that give thee interest ). Pi`el Perfect 3plural אֶתְכֶם וְנִשְּׁכוּ Jer 8:17 and they shall bite you fatally (figurative); Imperfect 3masculine plural אֶתהָֿעָם וַיְנַשְּׁכוּ Num 21:5 and they bit the people fatally(both of serpents). [ נָשַׁךְ ] verb denominative pay, give interest (compare Gerber Verba denominative 89 ); — Qal Imperfect 3masculine singular יִשָּׁ֑ךְ Deut 23:20 interest of anything off which one giveth interest (compare Dr). Hiph`il make one give interest; Imperfect 2masculine singular תַּשִּׁיךְ Deut 23:20 ( + accusative of congnate meaning with verb) 23:21 ; 23:21 , all with לְ person
